lrw.text: Lorwyn is a plane of kithkin, merrows, giants, faeries, boggarts, flamekin, elves, treefolk and changelings, and in this set it stands at the edge of change as the Great Aurora approaches.
Oona, fearing the Aurora, kills Maralen and replaces her body with a faerie vessel holding a mental duplicate, but the new Maralen becomes independent and turns against her creator.
Brigid takes the Crescent of Morningtide as the Great Aurora sweeps the world, transforming Lorwyn into Shadowmoor, where features correspond but are changed, such as Kinsbaile becoming Kinscaer.
Maralen eventually takes over as Queen of the Fae and restores the day and night cycle.

mor.text: In Morningtide, Lorwyn's evenings are brief, and its elves, with Rhys blamed for a cataclysmic event that killed many of them, hunt him with all their might to bring him to their vicious brand of justice.
Maralen sends the Vendilion clique on the gravest of tasks, and the clique lulls a party to sleep to read their thoughts, though it cannot breach Maralen's mind.

ecl.text: Years after the Phyrexian invasion, Lorwyn is a weakened plane in which elvish authority has collapsed and other species are reclaiming their ancestral lands, while pockets of Lorwyn sprout across Shadowmoor and throw the plane into turmoil.
Merrow flee into the deepest parts of the Wanderwine, and many flamekin hibernate underground, with around half returning as rimekin.
When Isilu wakes and stomps through Lorwyn, his presence turns day to night and neighbors against one another, and Brigid finds four stranded Arcavios students and leads them toward Goldmeadow.
Once the balance returns, Rhys is freed from his pact with Maralen and fades away into the daylight.
